bug_semantics: When the image proxy is enabled, an authenticated poster can place an attacker-chosen non-HTTPS URL in a BBCode [img] tag. SMF's BBCode renderer converts that URL into a local proxy.php URL and generates the required secret-derived hash itself. A subsequent request to that local URL makes the forum server fetch the remote URL. Before the fixes, the fetch path did not resolve and reject private, loopback, link-local, or other reserved destination addresses on the initial request and every redirect, so an attacker-controlled hostname or redirect could make SMF request internal services, including link-local metadata endpoints.
flaw_origin: The proxy fetch endpoint was already present in the immediate parent and required a secret-derived hash, but was not yet an attacker-usable signing oracle. Commit a892a53ba45330d69b8ad8b1ede82aebaa29537b completed the vulnerable mechanism by adding BBCode-renderer code that accepts the untrusted image URL and automatically emits /proxy.php?request=<url>&hash=md5(<url>.<secret>) without any destination-address validation. This is the smallest commit that made the pre-existing unvalidated server-side fetch reachable with a valid signature from attacker-controlled BBCode.
ai_marker: absent: the BIC commit object names Shitiz Garg <mail@dragooon.net> as both author and committer and contains only the human Signed-off-by: Shitiz Garg <mail@dragooon.net> trailer; there is no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, or other AI marker.
evidence: The assigned GHSA-9wvj-rhhh-8292 / CVE-2026-61520 advisory describes authenticated SSRF through the image proxy and names the two branch fix merges: https://github.com/SimpleMachines/SMF/commit/4bf35cf9e45573a5f55a6f52995086c1da89c096 for 3.0 and https://github.com/SimpleMachines/SMF/commit/b4d23dfd74a511587c605f9d294cefc3a75b4b26 for 2.1.

git show a892a53ba45330d69b8ad8b1ede82aebaa29537b shows a one-file, nine-line change in Sources/Subs.php. In both BBCode img validators it adds image_proxy_enabled/image_proxy_secret/boardurl and rewrites each non-HTTPS image to $boardurl . '/proxy.php?request=' . urlencode($data) . '&hash=' . md5($data . $image_proxy_secret).

git log -L 1283,1308:Sources/Subs.php a892a53ba45330d69b8ad8b1ede82aebaa29537b identifies a892a53ba45330d69b8ad8b1ede82aebaa29537b as the commit that added those automatic proxy-signing lines; git log -S'/proxy.php?request=' over Sources/Subs.php likewise returns a892a53ba45330d69b8ad8b1ede82aebaa29537b as the initial signing change. The later 72b01034c2773bff3a6b9be6b859acce1b79f19f commit merely moved the same behavior into get_proxied_url().

Immediate-parent verification: git show 5c923a26d6c55060efdaf4d489403b06de8f65a1:Sources/Subs.php at the two img validators shows only URL normalization and no proxy.php rewrite, no secret use, and no hash generation. git show/cat-file also confirms that the parent already contains proxy.php, whose checkRequest() verifies md5($request . $this->secret) and whose cacheImage() performs the server-side curl fetch. Thus the signing-oracle attack path is absent in the direct parent even though its inert, secret-gated sink exists.

Lifecycle cross-check: 72b01034c2773bff3a6b9be6b859acce1b79f19f extracted the rewrite into get_proxied_url(); 8cecdb815e845f83a63e688250296ce90f35fcce changed the proxy hash from MD5 to HMAC but preserved automatic signing; c33589c13f9cfff339d2fe6874dcf6b8f15f643b later rejected literal IP hosts and localhost but still did not resolve hostnames or validate redirect destinations, so attacker-controlled DNS/redirects retained the SSRF.

At the vulnerable 2.1 pre-fix tree 3c98cab9b6ca9c247da4b43d2879dcb61c0af568, Sources/Subs.php's [img] validator calls get_proxied_url(); get_proxied_url() creates a valid HMAC-signed proxy URL; proxy.php verifies that HMAC and cacheImage() calls fetch_web_data($request). The only destination checks compare the textual host against a literal IP, localhost, and the forum host, leaving DNS-resolved private/link-local targets and redirects unchecked.

The 3.0 advisory merge 4bf35cf9e45573a5f55a6f52995086c1da89c096 has first parent 57d30d5a0ec32073d0dd1fe5b038d41dd84171b3 and second-parent tip ce59add4bdcacea557fb9a9763ad4b24d75a8a48. The seven-commit fix branch starts at 6d8b5f2d5ddf14b26bf6e9e0812db9327770902d and ends at ce59add4bdcacea557fb9a9763ad4b24d75a8a48; its final tree is identical to the merge tree. It centralizes resolved-IP safety checks in WebFetchApi and revalidates redirect targets in the curl/socket fetchers.

The parallel 2.1 advisory merge b4d23dfd74a511587c605f9d294cefc3a75b4b26 has first parent 3c98cab9b6ca9c247da4b43d2879dcb61c0af568 and direct second parent 10a998ccbae25bd95d4c3857a66a30b018bb5fda; its merge tree equals the direct parent's tree. That patch adds is_fetch_safe(), calls it before fetch_web_data() connects, rechecks curl redirects, and invokes it from proxy.php.

Version-boundary checks with git merge-base --is-ancestor succeed for BIC a892a53ba45330d69b8ad8b1ede82aebaa29537b -> v2.1.0 and -> v3.0-alpha.1. The BIC is also contained in every listed stable tag through v2.1.7 and in v3.0-alpha.1 through v3.0-alpha.4. The checks v2.1.7 -> b4d23dfd74a511587c605f9d294cefc3a75b4b26 and v3.0-alpha.4 -> 4bf35cf9e45573a5f55a6f52995086c1da89c096 also succeed, placing each fix after the last vulnerable release tag present in the clone.

git cat-file commit a892a53ba45330d69b8ad8b1ede82aebaa29537b gives parent 5c923a26d6c55060efdaf4d489403b06de8f65a1, human author and committer Shitiz Garg <mail@dragooon.net>, subject 'Auto-transform non-HTTPS images into proxy link', and only a Signed-off-by trailer. The Claude Co-Authored-By trailer seen on later fix member 6d8b5f2d5ddf14b26bf6e9e0812db9327770902d is fix-only evidence and is excluded from BIC attribution under the protocol.
reasoning: The unvalidated fetch sink and the signing behavior arrived as separate granular commits. dcbaefb0976cf3e9d9490455bb59504d5c807847 created proxy.php, but the endpoint rejected requests without a secret-derived hash, so that precursor alone did not give a BBCode author the advisory's SSRF primitive. The direct parent of a892a53ba45330d69b8ad8b1ede82aebaa29537b still has exactly that secret-gated state. The BIC then made untrusted [img] URLs flow through a server-side signing oracle, producing a browser-loadable local proxy request that reaches the unvalidated server fetch. Later refactoring and stronger HMAC authentication retained that causal data flow, and the April 2026 textual-host checks remained bypassable because they did not validate resolved addresses or redirects. The June/July 2026 branch fixes close the mechanism at the fetch layer and on redirects, with corresponding advisory merges for 3.0 and 2.1. The BIC is a normal, non-merge, non-squash human commit, its direct parent lacks the signing flow, and its commit object has no AI authorship marker. Any AI marker on a 2026 fix commit is out of scope for BIC attribution. Therefore the closed verdict is NOT_AI.
